body.statement: Let \(H\) be symmetric and satisfy \(H_{ii}=0\) whenever no \(z\in Z\) has \(i\in O_z\), as well as the published Harshaw--Middleton--Savje pairwise design-compatibility criterion \(H_{ik}=0\) whenever \(i\ne k\) and no \(z\in Z\) has \(\{i,k\}\subseteq O_z\). Then \(h_H\in\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\subseteq\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,3}\). If also \(H-A\succeq0\), then \(h_H\in\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\). The inclusion of published Harshaw--Middleton--Savje conservative quadratic candidates satisfying these observability conditions in the Boolean quadratic cone is strict: the constant function with value \(1+\max_{\theta\in\Theta}f(\theta)\) belongs to \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\) but cannot equal any \(h_H\), since every homogeneous quadratic satisfies \(h_H(0)=0\). Consequently the inclusion in the Boolean quadratic/cubic comparison cone is also strict.
body.justification: This makes the theorem-level comparison exact: published design-compatible quadratic matrices embed into, but do not exhaust, the Boolean quadratic/cubic cone used by the witness certificate.
body.gap: Proposition 1 and Definitions 1--2 of \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} give the pairwise matrix criterion and positive-semidefinite conservativeness; they do not state the strict binary-cube inclusion into the all-observable comparison cone.
body.consumer: The exact \(55/36\) lower certificate can be applied to every published Harshaw--Middleton--Savje quadratic candidate without equating its smaller semidefinite program with the enlarged Boolean program.
body.proof_tex:
We prove the minimally corrected claim, including the necessary diagonal observability condition.  On \(\Theta\), binary idempotence and symmetry of \(H\) give
\[
 h_H(\theta)=\theta^\top H\theta
 =\sum_iH_{ii}\theta_i+2\sum_{i<k}H_{ik}\theta_i\theta_k. \tag{11}
\]
If \(H_{ii}\ne0\), the corrected hypothesis ensures that some \(O_z\) contains \(i\), so \(\{i\}\in\mathcal J\).  If \(H_{ik}\ne0\) for \(i\ne k\), pairwise design compatibility ensures that some \(O_z\) contains \(\{i,k\}\), so \(\{i,k\}\in\mathcal J\).  Every monomial in (11) is therefore observable and has degree at most two.  By \(\text{def:boolean-mobius-spaces}\),
\[
 h_H\in\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\subseteq\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,3}. \tag{12}
\]
If also \(H-A\succeq0\), then for every binary schedule
\[
 h_H(\theta)-f(\theta)=\theta^\top(H-A)\theta\ge0.
\]
Equations (12) and \(\text{def:bound-program}\) give
\(h_H\in\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\).

To prove strictness, put
\[
 C:=1+\max_{\theta\in\Theta}f(\theta).
\]
Finiteness of \(\Theta\) makes \(C\) finite, and \(f\ge0\) gives \(C\ge1\).  The constant function \(b_C(\theta)=C\) is generated by \(m_\varnothing\), so it lies in \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\), and \(b_C\ge f\), so it is conservative.  Yet \(h_H(0)=0\) for every homogeneous quadratic form, whereas \(b_C(0)=C>0\).  Hence no \(h_H\) equals \(b_C\).  The conservative compatible quadratic class is therefore a strict subset of the Boolean quadratic cone, and consequently also a strict subset of the Boolean degree-at-most-three comparison cone.
